findings.summary: The notes overstate receive-time duration estimates as upper bounds.
evidence: The release notes say pipe buffering makes command and phase durations upper bounds on executor timing.

StampingPipe timestamps lines when the reader receives them; it has no producer-side timestamps. Variable delay for the start and completion lines can make their receive-time difference either larger or smaller than the actual duration.
The timing tests supply fixed timestamps and do not verify that measured durations are upper bounds.
findings.action: Revise the claim to say receive-time deltas can understate or overstate producer timing. Do not recommend setting the progress window from them as though they were guaranteed upper bounds.

findings.summary: A short sink write can silently lose event bytes while capture reports complete.
evidence: StampingPipe._emit calls self._sink.write(data) but does not check its returned byte count.
capture() reports complete unless there is an error, an open writer at close, or dropped_bytes; a short write without an exception sets none of these.
The release notes promise that event bytes are never silently lost and the supplied pipe test uses BytesIO, which does not exercise short writes.
findings.action: Write until all bytes are accepted or record the unwritten remainder as dropped and the capture as incomplete; add a short-writing sink test.

findings.summary: A blocked log write can stop pipe draining and block the executor on a full pipe.
evidence: StampingPipe._emit writes and flushes synchronously on the same thread that drains the executor pipe.
If the sink write or flush stalls, _drain cannot read more bytes; the pipe can fill while the executor is writing.
The notes claim the reader keeps draining so the executor never blocks on a full pipe, but the supplied tests do not exercise a stalled sink.
findings.action: Qualify the no-blocking guarantee or change the capture path so a stalled sink cannot stop pipe draining, with any resulting loss recorded as incomplete.

counterweight_triage.concern: B1: a zero window disables loop checks as well as window checks.
counterweight_triage.disposition: The on_event guard returns before counting outcomes or feeding the timeline when window_seconds <= 0; the zero-window test checks both on_tick and repeated loop-family events.

counterweight_triage.concern: B2: a resumed Codex session that reuses an item id starts a separate command in --commands timing.
counterweight_triage.disposition: A repeated start allocates a new command key and updates the item-id mapping; the test verifies two starts, separate family counts, and only the resumed command's duration.

counterweight_triage.concern: A6: read-only Codex reviewers use read-only mode and drop the lane network config pair.
counterweight_triage.disposition: read_only_codex changes the sandbox value and removes only the exact lane network -c pair. The supplied self-review and brief-critique tests exercise the resulting command.

counterweight_triage.concern: Other release-note claims outside these findings.
counterweight_triage.disposition: The notes disclose that release tests check passed flags rather than an actual bind or fetch, and scope the debug-name collision and fallback caveats.

next_move: Correct the timing-bound claim and close or qualify the sink-write capture guarantees, then review the updated bound inputs.
